findings.body: In multiple places, the code converts a single DestinationCalendar object into an array containing that object (e.g., `destinationCalendar: booking.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : ...`). However, the type of `booking.destinationCalendar` is already an array (`DestinationCalendar[] | null`) as updated in the types and class definitions. Wrapping it again in an array results in a nested array (`DestinationCalendar[][]`), which is incorrect and will cause runtime errors when the code expects a flat array of DestinationCalendar objects.
findings.suggestion: Remove the extra array wrapping. Use `destinationCalendar: booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar || []` directly, assuming these are arrays already.
findings.title: Incorrect wrapping of destinationCalendar array causing nested arrays

findings.body: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the method `createAllCalendarEvents` iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` assuming it is an array, which is correct. However, in places where `destinationCalendar` is assigned from booking or user objects, the code sometimes wraps it again in an array, causing nested arrays. This inconsistency can cause bugs when accessing `destinationCalendar` as an array of DestinationCalendar objects.
findings.suggestion: Ensure that `destinationCalendar` is always assigned as an array of DestinationCalendar objects without extra wrapping. Remove redundant array wrapping when the source is already an array.
findings.title: Nested arrays due to redundant wrapping of destinationCalendar

findings.body: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, the code wraps `bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar` in an array even though its type is already an array, causing nested arrays. This will cause errors when downstream code expects a flat array of DestinationCalendar objects.
findings.suggestion: Assign `destinationCalendar` directly without wrapping in an array, e.g., `destinationCalendar: bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar || bookingToDelete.user.destinationCalendar || []`.
findings.title: Nested arrays due to redundant wrapping of destinationCalendar in handleCancelBooking

findings.body: In `packages/features/ee/payments/api/paypal-webhook.ts` and `packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts`, the code wraps `booking.destinationCalendar` in an array even though it is already an array, causing nested arrays. This will cause runtime errors when the calendar event expects a flat array.
findings.suggestion: Assign `destinationCalendar` directly without wrapping in an array, e.g., `destinationCalendar: booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar || []`.
findings.title: Nested arrays due to redundant wrapping of destinationCalendar in payment webhook handlers

findings.body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/loggedInViewer/deleteCredential.handler.ts` and other booking handlers, the code wraps `booking.destinationCalendar` in an array even though it is already an array, causing nested arrays. This will cause errors when the calendar event expects a flat array.
findings.suggestion: Assign `destinationCalendar` directly without wrapping in an array, e.g., `destinationCalendar: booking.destinationCalendar || booking.user?.destinationCalendar || []`.
findings.title: Nested arrays due to redundant wrapping of destinationCalendar in deleteCredential handler

findings.body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, and similar booking handlers, the code wraps `booking.destinationCalendar` or `bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar` in an array even though it is already an array, causing nested arrays.
findings.suggestion: Assign `destinationCalendar` directly without wrapping in an array, e.g., `destinationCalendar: booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar || []`.
findings.title: Nested arrays due to redundant wrapping of destinationCalendar in booking handlers

findings.body: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` and other calendar service implementations, the code correctly treats `destinationCalendar` as an array and accesses the first element or finds by credentialId. However, in some update and delete methods, the code uses `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` where `externalCalendarId` is used as a search key but can be null or undefined, which may cause unexpected behavior or always return undefined.
findings.suggestion: Add a null check for `externalCalendarId` before using it in `.find()`. For example, if `externalCalendarId` is falsy, fallback to a default calendar id.
findings.title: Potential incorrect calendar selection when externalCalendarId is null or undefined

findings.body: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code correctly treats `destinationCalendar` as an array and accesses the first element. This is consistent with the updated type. No issues found here.
findings.title: Correct handling of destinationCalendar as array in LarkCalendarService

findings.body: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, the `createEvent` function signature changed to accept an optional `externalId` parameter, and the call sites in `EventManager.ts` were updated accordingly. This is a backward-compatible change and improves calendar event creation by associating external calendar IDs. No issues found.
findings.title: Added externalId parameter to createEvent for better calendar event association

models.summary: The change updates the `destinationCalendar` property from a single object to an array of DestinationCalendar objects across many files. However, in many places, the code incorrectly wraps an already-array `destinationCalendar` in another array, causing nested arrays and likely runtime errors. This is a high-severity bug that needs fixing by removing redundant array wrapping. Other calendar service implementations correctly handle `destinationCalendar` as an array. Minor potential issue with null checks on externalCalendarId in calendar services.
